beats.trigger: Getting Going
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: With the right guardrails, you create output that's genuinely yours, not generic.
beats.got: A promise that the output will be mine. I'll see.

beats.trigger: Build a snake game as HTML.
beats.got: Homework, and a snake game. Not a business problem.

beats.trigger: **Package** the guardrails as reusable rules
beats.got: Bloom's verbs in a list. Same format as every programme.

beats.trigger: where did LLM output on your own work come out generic, and what made it feel like yours?
beats.got: A fair question. It's about my own work, not the future.

beats.trigger: The same question. Two answers. What makes the difference?
beats.got: A teaser slide. I can guess the answer.

beats.trigger: The first exchange became context.
beats.got: What I asked earlier changes what it answers later. Obvious once shown, and a clean demo.

beats.trigger: Change the front, change the back.
beats.got: It re-reads everything each time. I hadn't thought of it that way.

beats.trigger: You told the LLM who you are.
beats.got: Telling it a role shifts the answer. Fine, I can test that at my desk tonight.

beats.trigger: Tools, goals, checks, boundaries, and loops come later and depend on it.
beats.got: A framework with a list of parts, and later it gets bigger. I've seen this structure before.

beats.trigger: You write it once, and it shapes every answer.
beats.got: A file it reads at the start of every session. That's a concrete, practical idea.

beats.trigger: Change the context, watch the agent's output shift, then package what you learned for the next session.
beats.got: 45 minutes of doing, not listening. Better than slides.

beats.trigger: It works, but it's generic.
beats.got: A site built from my LinkedIn in minutes. Competent and bland, as they said it would be.

beats.trigger: not *"I should book a discovery call."*
beats.got: The site is meant to make colleagues want to work with me. A personal site, not a business case.

beats.trigger: The LLM already knows StoryBrand, so you don't reproduce the questions.
beats.got: I can name a framework I know and it applies it. That's useful for strategy work.

beats.trigger: The agent walks you through the five tuned beats.
beats.got: It interviews me and then rewrites. The questions are what improve it.

beats.trigger: Your strengths shape how the whole site sounds.
beats.got: I gave it five strengths and the tone shifted. Predictable.

beats.trigger: Most people can list what drives them mad at work in thirty seconds, but stall for five minutes on what they're great at.
beats.got: Easier to say what I hate. True, and I'm good at that list.

beats.trigger: "decks where every page says 'iterating'"
beats.got: My hate list (steering groups, transformation decks) made the page sound more like me than anything else so far.

beats.trigger: LLMs go easy on their own output.
beats.got: It flatters its own work and they say so openly. That's candid.

beats.trigger: *"Make it look like Stripe's design language"*
beats.got: I can name a site and it restyles in one go. Cheap fun, and it works.

beats.trigger: The chat summary rounds corners; the file is what travels
beats.got: It wrote my method into a file so another agent can repeat it. Useful in principle, I'd have to check it.

beats.trigger: The more specific the context, the more the output is yours.
beats.got: Specific input gives specific output. Fair, though not new as a principle.

beats.trigger: The same mechanism scales to business proposals, competitor analysis, compliance reviews and product strategy
beats.got: A claim that it scales. I haven't seen that yet.

beats.trigger: Iterate and Learn
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The move: change something, notice what shifted, adjust, build again.
beats.got: Plan-do-check-act again. I know this from lean.

beats.trigger: Grading its own work is another chance to be helpful
beats.got: It praises its own work because it was trained to be agreeable. A candid limit, stated plainly.

beats.trigger: Where it doesn't, yours counts.
beats.got: Treat its report as a claim and check it against what I saw. I can do that.

beats.trigger: Only you could catch a wrong line about you
beats.got: It's my judgment that makes it better, not the model's. That doesn't threaten anyone.

beats.trigger: Nobody knows where agents are going, not Anthropic, not your board.
beats.got: The big-picture speech. The admission that nobody knows is honest, the rest is the usual journey talk.

beats.trigger: Expect the generation rules to change a lot. The first pass is rarely right.
beats.got: Reviewing and sharpening the rules file. They admit the first pass is wrong.

beats.trigger: **compound interest on a rule file.**
beats.got: Repeat the loop and the file improves. The compound-interest line is a slogan, though.

beats.trigger: Your gut on what is uniquely you carries more weight than the agent's.
beats.got: Even a second reader goes soft, and my gut outranks it. Reassuring, and again candid.

beats.trigger: Your domain expertise is the test.
beats.got: Three bullets. I agree with them.

beats.trigger: Bring a live challenge and working access to Confluence and OneDrive.
beats.got: More homework. IT will need to give me access.

beats.trigger: Karpathy's LLM Wiki post; Lindenberg's memory-architecture piece, optional.
beats.got: Optional reading, which I'll skip.

beats.trigger: leave yourself a three-line readiness note.
beats.got: Prework with a deliverable. My calendar is already full.

beats.trigger: the biggest unresolved item is usually your challenge.
beats.got: Pick a real problem from my calendar. That's the right idea.

beats.trigger: If a connector needs admin approval, tell the training coordinator and keep going.
beats.got: Connecting it to company systems means GDPR and security questions, and the module doesn't address them.

beats.trigger: Before it writes anything, ask it for a plan and approve or revise it first.
beats.got: Ask for a plan and approve it before it changes files. Sensible control.

beats.trigger: If a line is blank, name a fallback; do not fill it with a plausible answer.
beats.got: Write down three lines and don't invent anything. Good advice for people too.

beats.trigger: a useful system is a living pile of text the agent can read, maintain, and improve.
beats.got: Memory is just text files. Less magic than I expected, which is fine.

beats.trigger: The output now travels with a file the agent re-reads next time.
beats.got: The file is what carries over between sessions.

take_homes: What I tell it first changes what it answers later, and I can put that in a file it reads every session.
It flatters its own work, so I check its self-assessment against what I know. My judgment is the test.
Starting from what I hate about work gave a better result than starting from my strengths.

monday.move: Rerun the hate-list exercise on one real document, such as a strategy memo or partner proposal, and see whether it reads less generic.
monday.when: Tuesday evening, 30 minutes, after the steering group
monday.stop_condition: If it's no better than what I'd have written by myself, I stop and file it as another fad.
monday.blocker: Calendar, and the unresolved question of putting company data into a US-hosted tool.

misconception.why: They said the model flatters itself and showed me the limit. That's the first candid thing, and it's more than agile or OKRs ever offered. I still don't know whether this scales beyond a personal site, so wait-and-see isn't dead yet.

one_line: First one in years that let me try something and admitted what doesn't work, but I haven't yet seen it do anything real for the business.
